scope: Сводка источников и consequential findings по inventory/DCFL/LL JSON. Это не аудит всего проекта и не подтверждение всех доказательств.

original_source_followup.work: William F. Ogden, A helpful result for proving inherent ambiguity (1968)
original_source_followup.locator: Math. Systems Theory 2, pp. 191-194; theorem/page locator не установлен
original_source_followup.read: Springer confirms title, author, issue, pages and DOI; the full text requires subscription.
original_source_followup.gap: Exact lemma quantifiers and theorem numbering were not checked. Do not label the original as read.

original_source_followup.work: Ogden, Ross, Winklmann, An 'Interchange Lemma' for Context-Free Languages (1985)
original_source_followup.locator: SIAM J. Comput. 14(2), pp. 410-415; exact lemma page/theorem not established
original_source_followup.read: SIAM abstract says the paper proves a necessary condition for CFLs and applies it to repetitive strings xyyz with nonempty y over alphabets of size at least three; DOI and pages verified.
original_source_followup.gap: The official page requires access for the article. Exact bounds/quantifiers in the interchange lemma remain supported by Hoogeboom slides, PDF p.116, a secondary source.

original_source_followup.work: Seymour Ginsburg and Sheila A. Greibach, Deterministic Context Free Languages (1966)
original_source_followup.locator: Information and Control 9(6), pp. 620-648; theorem/page locators not verified
original_source_followup.source_level: publisher DOI inaccessible; bibliographic records only
original_source_followup.read: No original article text read. The existing DCFL review records bibliographic metadata only at this DOI.
original_source_followup.gap: GG theorem numbering and MIN/MAX/inverse GSM hypotheses cannot be verified here. Do not upgrade related claims to original-source checked.

findings.finding: Hard classifier rules treat backreferences and nested recursion as nonregular; the rules need precise exceptions and language-level proof conditions.
findings.counterexample: (a)\1* denotes aa*, which is regular; S→aSb|aS|Sb|ε denotes a*b* despite nested recursion.
findings.source: Local finite-state/grammar constructions; inventory raised this as a review flag.

findings.finding: Finite pumping and finite Nerode searches cannot certify an unbounded theorem unless reported as finite evidence.
findings.counterexample: Checking finitely many pumping lengths, words or residual representatives does not quantify over all decompositions or all residuals.
findings.source: Inventory explicitly classifies these as bounded semantic checks.

findings.finding: The classifier's regularity heuristic for signed linear-combination thresholds is too broad; mixed signs can encode unbounded comparison.
findings.counterexample: {w : #a(w)-#b(w) >= 0} is nonregular; prefixes a^n and a^m, n<m, are distinguished by suffix b^m.
findings.source: Local Myhill-Nerode argument; inventory raised this as a high-priority flag.

findings.finding: The Ogden marked-position statement in THEORY cites a secondary source; Ogden's 1968 original was not read.
findings.source: Hoogeboom course slides PDF p.110, Lemma 4.3.1 (secondary). Springer DOI page confirms metadata only.

findings.finding: The interchange formula remains supported by secondary lecture notes; the 1985 original was opened only to its official abstract.
findings.source: Hoogeboom slides PDF p.116, Lemma 4.5.1 (secondary); SIAM official abstract confirms paper purpose, not exact lemma.

findings.finding: The two-word Yu pumping alternatives are stated as necessary, but the source actually read for that statement is Yamakami 2021 restating Yu, not Yu's 1989 original.
findings.counterexample: The old course witnesses fail to refute the full alternative; the audit records a separate proof for non-DCFL status.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.09383v3, PDF p.7 Lemma 3.2 statement read; proof dependencies not all checked. Yu original unread.

findings.finding: A Yu refutation must cover every permitted pumping decomposition; showing that one chosen decomposition fails is insufficient.
findings.counterexample: The old course witness for S does not refute Yu; a separate local proof establishes S is non-DCFL.
findings.source: Local universal marked-continuation proof, not original-source verification.

findings.finding: A DCFL has an infinite Nerode class; a non-DCFL proof via finite classes must establish finiteness for every class.
findings.counterexample: One infinite distinguishable family alone does not show that all Nerode classes are finite.
findings.source: Hoogeboom slides following Shallit, statement/sketch at PDF pp.113, 128-130; Shallit book proof unread.

findings.finding: Complement and right quotient by regular languages are listed as DCFL closures in the reviewed contract.
findings.source: Hoogeboom slides following Shallit, PDF pp.122, 128-130; secondary source, not original GG.

findings.finding: Inverse homomorphism (including erasing images), regular intersection, and left quotient by a fixed word were separately established by constructions; do not attribute them to unread GG text.
findings.counterexample: General left quotient by a regular language does not preserve DCFL; fixed-word left quotient is narrower.
findings.source: Local constructions in DCFL review; GG original unread.

findings.finding: DCFL languages are unambiguous; ambiguity of one supplied grammar does not prove its language is not DCFL.
findings.counterexample: An ambiguous CFG can describe a DCFL that also has another unambiguous grammar.
findings.source: Hoogeboom slides following Shallit, PDF pp.132-134; original GG proof unavailable.

findings.finding: LL(k) is a grammar property; language membership in the LL(k) class asks whether some LL(k) grammar generates it.
findings.counterexample: Failure of the supplied grammar's LL(k) table does not refute existence of another grammar for that language.
findings.source: Nijholt 1980, Definition 8.7, printed pp.109-110 / PDF pp.116-117; extracted and visually checked.

findings.finding: Ordinary LL(k) tests alternatives against the actual local continuation; global FOLLOW can combine incompatible occurrence contexts.
findings.counterexample: A global FOLLOW conflict need not be a local LL conflict at any occurrence.
findings.source: Nijholt 1980, Definitions 8.7/8.8, pp.109-110; director characterization Lemma 12.2, pp.212-213; fixed-point completeness proof is local.

findings.finding: Strong LL(k) and LL(k) differ at grammar level for k≥2; an equivalent strong grammar can be constructed by annotating nonterminals with finite right-context summaries.
findings.counterexample: S→aAaa | bAba, A→b | ε is LL(2) but not SLL(2); it passes SLL(3).
findings.source: Nijholt 1980 pp.109-110 and Theorem 10.4 pp.140-141 (PDF pp.116-117,147-148); one equivalent-cover step uses a local annotation justification because Nijholt cites RS.

findings.finding: Branch-point prefix bound was corrected: two words with common-prefix length ell yield a shared sentential form wδ with ell-k < |w| ≤ ell.
findings.counterexample: The old stronger bound fails for LL(1) S→a^100A, A→b|c when taking a one-character shared prefix.
findings.source: Local proof takes the first derivation step crossing ell-k; counterexample is recorded in LL JSON.

findings.finding: The union {a^n b^n}∪{a^n c^n} is DCFL but not LL(k) for any fixed k, separating the union of LL(k) classes from DCFL.
findings.counterexample: Mixing independently chosen b- and c-producing derivation components creates an impossible mixed word; reusing a (nonterminal, suffix-length) pair yields the contradiction.
findings.source: Local substitution proof plus explicit DPDA; no external source claimed.

findings.finding: Left-recursion elimination must preserve empty-language cases and detect nullable-prefix hidden recursion.
findings.counterexample: S→Sa has empty language but the old transform produced a*; S→ASa|a with A→ε can retain hidden left recursion.
findings.source: Exact grammar counterexamples and fixes documented in LL review; implementation verification is separate.

findings.finding: Sample absence and oracle None/exception cannot certify nonmembership or equivalence; only conclusive negative membership can refute a candidate word.
findings.counterexample: S→A^30, A→ε and S→ε both generate {ε}, but a capped sentential-form sampler returned false.
findings.source: Local counterexample; review recommends CNF+CYK for refuting apparent CFG mismatches and still labels positive sample checks bounded.

findings.finding: Do not add blanket undecidability or further LL closure claims without theorem-level verification; current contract limits itself to fixed-k decision and explicit counterexamples.
findings.source: RS1970 and AU1972 full texts were not obtained; no original theorem locator verified.

global_boundaries: Hoogeboom slide locators already in THEORY_REFERENCE remain secondary: PDF p.110 for Ogden and p.116 for interchange.
Official primary publisher pages were found for the three requested works, but none yielded accessible full original text; metadata/abstracts do not verify exact theorem formulations.
proved_locally means a written local argument, not a proof assistant certificate or source-checked theorem.
Python tests and finite experiments do not establish universal language claims or full implementation equivalence.
This is a targeted evidence summary, not proof of the whole project or all four pipelines.
